root.name: French Defense: Guimard Variation, Thunderbunny Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 Nc6 4. c3 dxe4 5. Nxe4 e5

overview: In the Guimard (3.Nd2 Nc6) Black prepares ...e5 and avoids the ordinary Tarrasch pawn structures. After 4.c3 dxe4 5.Nxe4 e5 (the Thunderbunny) Black hits the centre at once, aiming for equality; White can take on e5 or play Nf3 with an open game. The ideas are simple but the early ...e5 break leaves Black's king in the centre.

white_ideas.idea: Exchange or take on e5 and develop with Nf3 and Bd3
Use the lead in development and the open e-file

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...e5 and develop with ...Bg4 and ...Nf6
Trade pieces and reach equal endings

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after ...e5 and dxe5 or dxe5/Nxe5

character.notes: The early ...e5 break gives open, fairly tactical play but not forcing.

character.reason: An open but not forcing French sideline.

approach.reason: Less common but a respectable line.

plans.reason: White tries to use the lead in development after the e-file opens.
